newsitem.title: USA: Garcia Abrego conviction will not stem drug flow.
newsitem.headline: Garcia Abrego conviction will not stem drug flow.

text.p: The conviction of drug kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego should put a scare in Mexican druglords, but will not stem the flow of drugs smuggled across the U.S.-Mexico border, U.S. agents said on Wednesday.
Other drug traffickers are already stepping into the void left by the destruction of Garcia Abrego's notorious Gulf cartel, they said in a press conference.

"This is going to send a chill to the drug trafficking community in Mexico," said Don Ferrarone, a special agent with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. "Major traffickers are not happy to see this (conviction)."
But, he said, "They've already had a certain regrouping that's gone on" since Garcia Abrego's arrest in January, meaning the flow of drugs would not diminish.
Ferrarone said a drug cartel based in Ciudad Juarez, allegedly headed by Amado Carrillo Fuentes, had replaced the Gulf cartel as the biggest drug trafficking organisation in Mexico.
"Amado Carrillo Fuentes is clearly the one in charge now," he said.
Garcia Abrego, 52, was convicted on Wednesday by a federal jury on 22 drug trafficking, money laundering and conspiracy charges and faces up to life in prison.
Even if the conviction has no effect on the quantity of drugs flowing across the border, it was a big win, officials said, because Garcia Abrego was such a big fish.
"This was a very, very important case," said U.S. Attorney Gaynelle Griffin Jones.

FBI special agent Chris Swecker said the dimensions of the chase were such that five different federal agencies, working with local and Mexican officials, made 35 seizures of drugs and money as they pursued Garcia Abrego for 10 years before catching him.
The reason, Ferrarone said, was simple.

"He caused a great deal of families and kids and adults in this country and all into Mexico, as well as deep into South America, to suffer. I can't see any better punishment for him than to have to go away (to prison) forever," he said.
